narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Official Timing Dossier"**

The demo is a race weekend's paperwork, not a gamer HUD. Each generation is a session with its own classification sheet; the track is the circuit map from a race programme, printed on light-blue graph paper; the standings tower is a timing screen set in heavy condensed numerals. Everything sits on white paper in LAMIA navy ink, with teal as the second ink and orange reserved for whoever is leading.

Density is split in two. The first viewport (map about two thirds wide, tower on the right, one-line bulletin under the map, presenter toolbar below) is sparse and huge so it reads from 3 m on a TV. The appendix below the fold (experiment sliders, champion vault, seed, keyboard shortcuts) is ordinary document density for the presenter only, and presentation mode hides it entirely.

The world rejects the dark neon gamer/HUD dashboard. It is light theme only, by brand commitment.
keyCharacteristics: White paper, navy ink, ruled tables; no dark surfaces except the asphalt ribbon and the selected-car chips.
Saira Condensed 800 for every number that matters, always tabular.
The teal/orange double rule from the LAMIA logo as the signature divider.
Orange marks the leader or the fastest thing, red marks a crash or a mutation, and nothing else.
Everything scales in `vh` in presentation mode; nothing important is smaller than about 2vh there.

rules.name: The One Leader Rule
rules.body: Orange means "best right now". One car, P1, the clock and the bullet. If two things are orange on the map, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Red Is Loss Rule
rules.body: Red appears only where something was lost or changed by chance: a crash, an error, a kerb, a mutation. Never for emphasis.

rules.name: The Paper Only Rule
rules.body: Light theme only. Dark fills are limited to asphalt, the navy chip, and the elite tag.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every live number (generation, timer, laps, record, car numbers, seed) sets `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` so the tower does not jitter while it updates.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Condensed Rule
rules.body: A number the audience should read goes in Saira Condensed at 700 or 800. Sentences never do.

rules.name: The Three Metres Rule
rules.body: In presentation mode every text size has a vh term and a floor of at least 12px; anything the audience needs is sized as a share of the screen height, not in fixed pixels.

rules.name: The Paper On Paper Rule
rules.body: Shadows are always navy-tinted, soft and negative-spread, and only on something laid over the page or the map. Tables, controls and the tower stay flat and use rules instead.

dos: **Do** set every live number in Saira Condensed 700/800 with tabular numerals.
**Do** use the brand double rule (teal over orange, offset) to open a sheet or page.
**Do** separate data with horizontal rules (rule, rule-2), with a heavier navy rule at the start of a block.
**Do** use orange-ink, not orange, when the leader's color has to be text on paper.
**Do** give every text size a vh-based clamp in presentation mode.
**Do** back every car color with a legend or a text label; color alone never identifies a role.
donts: **Don't** use a dark background, neon glows or a HUD look; this is light theme only.
**Don't** use orange or red for emphasis, decoration or a generic call to action.
**Don't** add shadows to flat controls, tables or the tower; shadows are only for paper laid over something.
**Don't** set sentences in the condensed face or numbers in the body face.
**Don't** redefine the palette per renderer; the canvas renderers repeat the CSS hex values and must stay in sync with them.
